pages.moment: They have just stepped out of their car in the underground car park — the silver car is parked right behind them. HAON holds his MOTHER's hand tightly and bounces up on his toes, mid-jump, tugging her hand forward toward the lift door, mouth open in an excited 'Hurry, Mum, hurry!'. The MOTHER is being pulled along a step, laughing and looking down at him.

Still in the car park, just before going up to Grandma's home. HAON has just been dressed in his new hanbok and twirls round on one foot, arms held out to the sides so the jeogori swings, looking at his MOTHER with eyes curved into happy half-moons — 'Look at me! Don't I look nice?'. The MOTHER crouches down in front of him, smiling proudly and clapping, an open bag at her feet with a folded cloth spilling out.

The GRANDMOTHER sits cross-legged on the patterned floor cushion in the middle of the room. HAON is snuggled right in her lap, leaning back against her. Her arms come around him and her two hands hold an open picture book in front of both of them. She looks down at the page, reading aloud with a gentle smile. Haon has turned his head up toward her face, eyes sparkling, asking 'Grandma, what happens next?'. Warm daylight from the paper-screen window falls on them and the book.

Evening after dinner; the window is dark night. On the low wooden table there are empty rice bowls and little side-dish bowls. HAON sits on the floor cushion with his legs stretched out, patting his round, full tummy with both hands and laughing, looking up at his GRANDMOTHER. The GRANDMOTHER kneels beside him, smiling fondly down at him, one hand resting on his back.

Morning in the kitchen. On the wooden table: a bowl of rice, a plate of golden fried-tofu pockets, and an open YELLOW square lunchbox, half full of neat yubu-chobap rice pockets. HAON stands on tiptoe at the table with grains of rice stuck to his fingertips, carefully pressing one more rice pocket into the yellow lunchbox, bouncing with excitement — 'Mum, let's go!'. The MOTHER stands right beside him leaning in, holding another rice pocket, smiling down at him.

On the wooden pier. The big white ferry waits at the water's edge. HAON holds a small yellow lunchbox and looks all around with wide, puzzled eyes — 'Mum, where is the bus?'. The MOTHER stands close beside him, one hand on his shoulder, and with the other she points at the big white ferry, laughing — 'This boat IS the Han River Bus!'. Haon is just turning to follow her pointing finger toward the boat.

On the ferry deck, gliding over the sparkling river. HAON stands at the blue railing holding it with both hands, face lifted into the breeze, the wind pushing his top, his eyes curved into happy half-moons as he laughs — 'Mum, the wind feels so good!'. The MOTHER stands right beside him with a hand on his back, her long hair blowing, smiling at him.

Late afternoon, the sky beginning to glow warm orange and pink over the river. In the shade of the tree, the MOTHER and HAON sit together on a picnic mat on the grass, the open yellow lunchbox full of rice pockets between them. Haon has his cheeks puffed full and is laughing with a rice pocket in his hand; the MOTHER laughs with him, holding a rice pocket too. A small red child's bicycle lies on the grass nearby.

On the open-top upper deck of the double-decker bus, the family has just sat down on the front bench seat, HAON between his MOTHER and FATHER. Haon tips his head right back and stares straight up at the wide-open blue sky, eyes round and mouth open — 'Whoa, there's no roof!' — pointing up with one hand. His MOTHER and FATHER are laughing at his surprise, looking at him.

The bus is moving. The wind blows through HAON's hair. He sits on the bench seat between his parents, turned toward his FATHER with an excited, heart-pounding face. His FATHER leans toward him and points into the distance, telling him about the palace they are going to see. His MOTHER smiles at them both. Green Namsan mountain and the tower drift by in the background.

Just inside the palace courtyard. HAON has stopped dead in his tracks, eyes round with wonder — 'Is this... the olden days?'. Around the courtyard in the middle distance are a few visitors in colourful hanbok: a little girl in a pink jeogori, a man in a blue robe, a child with a flower in her hair. His MOTHER and FATHER stand just behind Haon, smiling at his amazement, his mother's hand on his shoulder.

The MOTHER holds HAON's hand tightly and the family walks together into the courtyard toward the great palace hall, seen from behind at a three-quarter angle. Haon looks up at his mother and nods, taking a big step forward; the FATHER walks at their side. Their long soft shadows fall on the paving stones.
